title: Wholeness Goal Brainstorm
opening: Look at the life your goals include and what they leave out. Decide whether an omission is unwanted, then choose a goal, a changed arrangement or protected participation where it helps.

labels.comparison: Protect friendship without turning it into a score
labels.comparisonIntro: A person protects work and training time but leaves no room for ordinary time with friends. Compare that unwanted omission with a deliberate short period of focus before deciding what needs to change.
labels.adherenceText: Work and training receive time and attention. A goal list can make sense item by item while collectively leaving out something valued.
labels.valueText: Missing friend time may be an unwanted imbalance, or a deliberate temporary focus. Inspect actual experience and values; an empty category alone does not establish a defect.
labels.outcomeText: Protect an unstructured evening with friends if that serves the life intended. Participation need not become a friendship performance metric; check whether the new arrangement supports it.
labels.signalQuestion: Choose a part of the comparison
labels.rhythmTitle: A fuller life does not require a target for everything
labels.rhythmText: Consider relevant life dimensions and paired experiences without forcing every category into a goal. Do not manufacture adversity or score your wholeness. A narrow season can be deliberate. If a new target crowds out the experience it was meant to support, change its form.
labels.practiceIntro: Use only the fields that clarify your question. A partial private note is fine; observations, assumptions and desired outcomes need not be complete before you can keep them.
labels.private: This optional private reflection is separate from the six required assessment questions.

labels.sourceQuote:
Wholeness Goal Brainstorm
Examine which life dimensions and paired experiences your goals include or leave
out. Choose where a goal could address a real imbalance.

example.qualities: Keep progressing at work and train three evenings each week.
example.contribution: Achievement, skill development and physical activity.
example.present: The current pattern has lasted months and I miss ordinary shared time. It is not just a chosen short work season.
example.connection: Protect one evening without a performance target; discuss a suitable time with friends.
example.change: Notice whether we can spend time together without the new arrangement adding pressure or crowding out rest.
